app.js:43 importRecipes is dead code and would produce bad records if it were used. Nothing calls it. If it were wired up, it would not trim names or skip blank lines. app.js:33 The delete handler calls describe(r) without checking that the recipe was found. The comment on line 14 says r is never null, but loadRecipes does not guarantee that. localStorage holds [{"name":"x","minutes":5}] with no id, or with a numeric id. The li renders with data-id="undefined" or a string id, and recipes.find(x => x.id === id) returns undefined. Clicking Delete throws "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'name')" inside describe, so the entry can never be removed. Duplicate ids also make find return the wrong recipe.

app.js:21 parseInt silently truncates decimals, and the JS never enforces the HTML max of 600. Entering 1.5 stores 1 minute. Entering 0.5 parses to 0 and shows 'Give the recipe a name...' even though the field has a value. The max=600 limit is enforced only by the browser form check, so it is bypassed whenever submit validation is skipped.

store.js:54 A JSON.parse failure or blocked storage returns [] with no message, although the comment says app.js tells the user. app.js never does. The stored value is corrupt or truncated. The app starts empty and shows 'No recipes yet'. The next add or delete calls saveRecipes and overwrites the corrupt value, so recoverable data is lost permanently and the user was never warned.

app.js:66 A recipe loaded from storage can lack a valid id, so the delete handler's find returns undefined and describe(undefined) throws. loadRecipes only checks typeof r.name === 'string'. A stored entry like {"name":"x","minutes":5} with no id renders data-id="undefined". dataset.id is then the string 'undefined', which never equals the real undefined id, so r is undefined. Clicking Delete throws a TypeError inside describe (line 49), and the entry can never be removed. The comment on line 48 claims r is never null, which is wrong.

Edge cases, not flagged: a hand-edited or corrupt localStorage entry could make totalMinutes concatenate strings. Delete ignores a failed save. Both depend on specific input or state, so I held back under the review's high-signal rule.

app.js:23 Each tab keeps its own in-memory copy and saves the whole list, so a second tab erases the first tab's recipes. Driven with two pages in one browser context, both loaded empty. app.js:21 parseInt on a number input stores "1e2" (a valid 100) as 1 minute. styles.css:4 A long unbroken recipe name forces sideways scrolling at 390 px. The list item has no overflow-wrap or min-width rule. app.js:74 The 'shortcut' comment promises a few hundred recipes of headroom, but render rebuilds the whole innerHTML on every change and has no virtualization or measurement behind that figure. The threshold is an unmeasured claim in a comment. With large imported or stored lists, each add or delete re-renders the entire list.

util.js:15 getJson is unused, and its fetch contradicts the README's 'nothing is sent anywhere'. It is dead code that adds network capability to an app documented as offline-only. A reviewer checking the privacy claim would have to rule it out. Remove it.
